abstract: Invariant-aware validators can outperform structural baselines on constructed errors without establishing their performance against independently supplied corrections. We audit two finite synthetic designs and add a predeclared study on three external reference datasets. A separate metric implementation reproduces 195 overall comparisons in the synthetic artifacts. Exact finite score-group Brier decomposition attributes lower Brier to higher resolution even as empirical reliability worsens; perfect binary decisions give zero Brier and ECE. One statistic signature among 64 clusters explains degenerate resampling in the first design, while the second has six signatures among 48 clusters. The external study evaluates 11,144 cells using four fixed rule-attribution policies, with calibration-only lookup and 10,000 paired component-bootstrap replicates. On Flights, flagging every participant in a dependency conflict rejects 74.4% of reference-correct cells. A minority-value policy reduces this to 8.0% while accepting 12.2% of reference-incorrect cells. The prediction that lookup improves minority-policy Brier across all three datasets is mixed: the Flights interval crosses zero. The findings distinguish constraint-conflict detection, error localization and probability scoring. They constitute a reproducible case study, not a new detector, a causal transfer experiment or population performance evidence.
title: Auditing Invariant Validation Benchmarks: Construction, Error Attribution, and Probability Scores
